blurbPl: Dział Życie prywatne na maturę rozszerzoną: rodzina, relacje, rutyna i czas wolny. Fiszki ENG–PL.
blurbEn: Extended Matura private life: family, relationships, routines and leisure.

items.definitionEn: a family in which parents and children from previous relationships live together
items.example: A blended family needs patience while new routines form.

items.definitionEn: the person legally recognised as your closest family member
items.example: Write your next of kin on the hospital form.

items.definitionEn: competition or jealousy between brothers and sisters
items.example: Teachers often see sibling rivalry when one child gets more praise.

items.definitionEn: two parents and their children living as one household
items.example: The advert showed a nuclear family around a Sunday table.

items.definitionEn: a household in which one parent brings up the children
items.example: A single-parent family may rely on grandparents for childcare.

items.definitionEn: a family that cares for a child who is not legally theirs
items.example: The boy settled well with his foster family.

items.definitionEn: an adult who has legally become a child's parent
items.example: An adoptive parent has the same duties as a biological one.

items.definitionEn: the person whose wage mainly supports the household
items.example: After the factory closed, she became the only breadwinner.

items.definitionEn: a person who relies on someone else for money or care
items.example: Each child counts as a dependent until they finish school.

items.definitionEn: the way a child is raised and taught at home
items.example: A strict upbringing does not suit every teenager.

items.definitionEn: the family of your husband or wife
items.example: We spend Christmas with my in-laws every other year.

items.definitionEn: a husband or wife
items.example: Please give the full name of your spouse.

items.definitionEn: a man who is engaged to be married
items.example: Her fiancé proposed during a walking holiday in Scotland.

items.definitionEn: a woman who is engaged to be married
items.example: He introduced his fiancée to the whole extended family.

items.definitionEn: a woman whose husband has died
items.example: The widow still wears her wedding ring.

items.definitionEn: a man whose wife has died
items.example: The widower moved closer to his daughter.

items.definitionEn: a person related to you who is born later, such as a grandchild
items.example: She is a descendant of farmers who left the village in 1900.

items.definitionEn: a person in your family who lived a long time ago
items.example: He researched an ancestor who fought in the war.

items.definitionEn: a person's child or children
items.example: Protective parents find it hard to let their offspring move out.

items.definitionEn: the state of being related by blood or marriage
items.example: In a crisis, kinship still shapes who people turn to.

items.definitionEn: the emotional and practical bonds between relatives
items.example: Even after emigration, family ties remained strong.

items.definitionEn: a gathering of relatives who do not usually all meet
items.example: Cousins flew in from Dublin for the family reunion.

items.definitionEn: no longer in contact or on friendly terms with a relative
items.example: He has been estranged from his father for a decade.

items.definitionEn: the member of a family who is seen as a disappointment
items.example: Every family joke treats him as the black sheep.

items.definitionEn: having strong, loyal relationships within a group
items.example: They grew up in a close-knit neighbourhood.

items.definitionEn: a family whose relationships are regularly harmful or chaotic
items.example: The novel portrays a dysfunctional family without cheap drama.

items.definitionEn: your parents, children, brothers and sisters, and usually your spouse
items.example: Only immediate family may visit in the evenings.

items.definitionEn: an adult who promises to support a child, often at a christening
items.example: A godparent is expected to stay in the child's life.

items.definitionEn: a person with the legal right to care for a child
items.example: Her aunt became her legal guardian after the accident.

items.definitionEn: a person who will receive property when someone dies
items.example: The farm will pass to the eldest heir.

items.definitionEn: to receive money or property from someone who has died
items.example: They will inherit the cottage if the will is valid.

items.definitionEn: a legal document saying who should receive your property after death
items.example: She updated her last will after the second child was born.

items.definitionEn: a valuable object passed down through generations
items.example: The clock is a family heirloom from her great-grandmother.

items.definitionEn: the social and family circumstances you grow up in
items.example: Universities should not judge you only on family background.

items.definitionEn: beliefs about how relatives should treat one another
items.example: His speech about family values felt old-fashioned to the teens.

items.definitionEn: the people who live together in one home, and that home as a unit
items.example: Everyone in the household shares the cooking on weekdays.

items.definitionEn: a brother or sister with whom you share only one parent
items.example: She met her half-sibling for the first time at sixteen.

items.definitionEn: a family member you are not closely related to
items.example: A distant relative left her a small sum of money.

items.definitionEn: adults who care for their children and their ageing parents at once
items.example: The sandwich generation often has little time left for hobbies.

items.definitionEn: mothers and fathers who need more support as they grow old
items.example: He visits his ageing parents every Sunday without fail.

items.definitionEn: a person whose main work is running the home rather than paid employment
items.example: Being a homemaker is work, even when it is unpaid.

items.definitionEn: a mother or father who looks after children instead of going out to work
items.example: A stay-at-home parent still needs adult conversation.

items.definitionEn: a long, bitter quarrel between relatives
items.example: The family feud started over a piece of land.

items.definitionEn: to resemble an older relative in looks or character
items.example: People say I take after my grandfather when I lose my temper.

items.definitionEn: to admire and respect someone
items.example: Many younger cousins look up to her because she is honest.

items.definitionEn: to continue communicating with someone
items.example: Old classmates promised to keep in touch after graduation.

items.definitionEn: to have a friendly relationship with someone
items.example: I get on with my stepmother better than I expected.

items.definitionEn: to stop being friendly after an argument
items.example: He used to fall out with his brother over borrowed clothes.

items.definitionEn: to become friends again after a quarrel
items.example: She wants to make up with her sister before the wedding.

items.definitionEn: to end a romantic relationship
items.example: They decided to break up after months of silence.

items.definitionEn: to end a relationship or marriage; to start living apart
items.example: My parents split up when I was twelve.

items.definitionEn: to have a romantic relationship with someone
items.example: She used to go out with a boy from the sixth form.

items.definitionEn: to invite someone to go on a date
items.example: He is too shy to ask out anyone from his course.

items.definitionEn: in serious difficulty, especially a relationship
items.example: Their engagement looked on the rocks after the row.

items.definitionEn: to get married
items.example: They plan to tie the knot in a small village church.

items.definitionEn: to go to the front of a church or venue to get married
items.example: She will walk down the aisle with her father.

items.definitionEn: a male friend who supports the groom at a wedding
items.example: The best man forgot the rings for a dreadful minute.

items.definitionEn: a female friend who supports the bride at a wedding
items.example: Her sister will be maid of honour at the ceremony.

items.definitionEn: an agreement to get married; the period before the wedding
items.example: They announced their engagement at a family dinner.

items.definitionEn: to live together as a couple without being married
items.example: Many couples cohabit for years before they marry.

items.definitionEn: a period when a couple lives apart to test whether the relationship can continue
items.example: They agreed a trial separation rather than a sudden divorce.

items.definitionEn: the legal right to care for a child after parents separate
items.example: The court granted her custody of both children.

items.definitionEn: money paid by a parent to help raise a child they do not live with
items.example: He pays child maintenance on the first of every month.

items.definitionEn: to move out of your parents' home and live independently
items.example: Not every twenty-year-old is ready to leave the nest.

items.definitionEn: the situation when children have moved out and parents remain at home
items.example: They found the empty nest strangely quiet at first.

items.definitionEn: a person you feel uniquely close to, often romantically
items.example: She does not believe everyone has one soulmate.

items.definitionEn: a person who shares your attitudes and feelings
items.example: I recognised a kindred spirit as soon as we started talking.

items.definitionEn: a person who is a friend of both you and someone else
items.example: They met through a mutual friend at a birthday meal.

items.definitionEn: someone who is kind only when life is easy
items.example: A fair-weather friend disappears the moment you need help.

items.definitionEn: a person you spend time with and who keeps you company
items.example: After retirement he wanted a companion for long walks.

items.definitionEn: the small group of people you trust most
items.example: Only her inner circle knew about the engagement.

items.definitionEn: to avoid socialising much and stay private
items.example: The new lodger prefers to keep himself to himself.

items.definitionEn: to tell someone private thoughts because you trust them
items.example: She can confide in her aunt, but not in her classmates.

items.definitionEn: a person who listens and comforts you when you are upset
items.example: Everyone needs a shoulder to cry on during the exam season.

items.definitionEn: to become friends again after a quarrel
items.example: They make it up with each other before the family dinner starts.

items.definitionEn: wanting to control a partner or friend and their time
items.example: A possessive boyfriend checked her messages every hour.

items.definitionEn: giving help and encouragement in a kind way
items.example: She is lucky to have a supportive partner during exams.

items.definitionEn: to fail to appreciate someone or something because they always seem available
items.example: Do not take for granted the parent who drives you everywhere.

items.definitionEn: to become less close gradually, without a big argument
items.example: Old school friends often drift apart after university.

items.definitionEn: to talk with someone you have not seen and hear their news
items.example: I must catch up with my cousin before she goes abroad.

items.definitionEn: to agree with someone; to share the same opinion
items.example: I do not see eye to eye with my father about curfews.

items.definitionEn: to like someone immediately and get on well
items.example: They hit it off on the first day of college.

items.definitionEn: to share interests, values or experiences
items.example: We have a lot in common, so the friendship grew quickly.

items.definitionEn: to repair a relationship after a quarrel
items.example: They managed to patch things up before Christmas dinner.

items.definitionEn: willing to talk to someone after a disagreement
items.example: They are barely on speaking terms after the argument.

items.definitionEn: unfriendly behaviour that shows you are ignoring someone
items.example: She gave her former friend the cold shoulder at the party.

items.definitionEn: not becoming too close or involved
items.example: He keeps new housemates at arm's length until he trusts them.

items.definitionEn: close and affectionate but not romantic or sexual
items.example: Theirs is a platonic friendship and they want it to stay that way.

items.definitionEn: the decision to stay loyal to a person or a relationship
items.example: Marriage requires commitment, not only a party.

items.definitionEn: the ability of two people to live or work together well
items.example: They tested their compatibility on a long cycling holiday.

items.definitionEn: having a romantic or sexual relationship outside your partnership
items.example: She left him when she discovered he had been unfaithful.

items.definitionEn: the process of becoming friends or partners again after a serious quarrel
items.example: Their reconciliation took months of honest conversations.

items.definitionEn: to be the person who makes the main decisions in a relationship
items.example: Friends joke that she is the one to wear the trousers at home.

items.definitionEn: to do the same job or live in a similar way as someone older
items.example: She refused to follow in their footsteps and became a designer.

items.definitionEn: an adult who returns to live with parents after living away
items.example: High rents have made the boomerang child a common figure in cities.

items.definitionEn: a very noticeable likeness between two people
items.example: There is a striking resemblance between the twins and their uncle.

items.definitionEn: a regular, often boring job that must be done at home
items.example: Loading the dishwasher is the chore nobody wants.

items.definitionEn: time spent giving someone your full attention
items.example: Phones stay in the kitchen during quality time after dinner.

items.definitionEn: to go out to do small practical jobs such as shopping or posting a parcel
items.example: I run errands for my grandmother on Saturday mornings.

items.definitionEn: the tiring, repetitive routine of everyday life
items.example: A short walk helps her survive the daily grind.

items.definitionEn: full of busy, rushed activity
items.example: Monday mornings are always hectic in our flat.

items.definitionEn: done slowly, without rushing
items.example: Sunday breakfast is a leisurely meal in our house.

items.definitionEn: a person who prefers to stay up late
items.example: A night owl finds 7 a.m. lectures painful.

items.definitionEn: a person who likes to get up and start early
items.example: An early bird can finish housework before the others wake.

items.definitionEn: a plan for how a household will spend its money
items.example: They keep a household budget in a shared notebook.

items.definitionEn: to divide housework fairly among the people who live together
items.example: Flatmates should share the chores, not leave them to one person.

items.definitionEn: to delay tasks you ought to do
items.example: If you put things off all week, Sunday becomes miserable.

items.definitionEn: able to pay for your own life without help from parents
items.example: She wanted to be financially independent before she turned twenty-five.

items.definitionEn: to leave your parents' home and live elsewhere
items.example: He will move out when his first salary arrives.

items.definitionEn: a person who shares a rented house with you
items.example: A tidy housemate is worth more than a cheap room.

items.definitionEn: an extra bedroom used for visitors or a tenant
items.example: They turned the spare room into a study during lockdown.

items.definitionEn: the physical and emotional room you need around yourself
items.example: Teenagers guard their personal space, including a locked bedroom.

items.definitionEn: the state of not being watched or interrupted
items.example: A thin wall leaves little privacy in a student house.

items.definitionEn: too interested in other people's private lives
items.example: A nosy neighbour asked why the lights were on at midnight.

items.definitionEn: trying too hard to keep someone from any risk or independence
items.example: Some overprotective parents can make leaving home feel frightening.

items.definitionEn: not strict; allowing more freedom than usual
items.example: A lenient curfew still has to be taken seriously.

items.definitionEn: resisting rules and authority, especially as a teenager
items.example: A rebellious phase does not mean a child rejects the whole family.

items.definitionEn: a young person between childhood and adulthood; typical of that age
items.example: An adolescent needs both boundaries and a chance to decide.

items.definitionEn: a time by which you must be home in the evening
items.example: Her curfew on school nights is ten o'clock.

items.definitionEn: to keep complaining or reminding someone in an annoying way
items.example: Parents nag about dirty cups because nobody else notices them.

items.definitionEn: to deal with several responsibilities at the same time
items.example: She has to juggle revision, a part-time job and family meals.

items.definitionEn: to start living a calmer, more stable life, often with a partner
items.example: His aunts keep asking when he will settle down.

items.definitionEn: to make a place your long-term home
items.example: After three cities they wanted to put down roots near their parents.

items.definitionEn: taking great care that your home looks clean and attractive
items.example: A house-proud host notices every crumb on the carpet.

items.definitionEn: to have just enough money for basic needs
items.example: A single income made it hard to make ends meet.

items.definitionEn: having plenty of money; comfortably rich
items.example: A well-off relative paid for the driving lessons.

items.definitionEn: allowed too much and therefore badly behaved or ungrateful
items.example: A spoilt child expects a new gadget every month.

items.definitionEn: to fail to give someone or something the care they need
items.example: Do not neglect old friendships when a new relationship starts.

items.definitionEn: the process of becoming emotionally closer
items.example: Cooking together is simple bonding after a hard week.

items.definitionEn: a childhood with many rules and little freedom
items.example: A strict upbringing taught him punctuality, but not how to relax.

items.definitionEn: a childhood in which a person was protected from ordinary difficulties
items.example: A sheltered childhood can make university feel overwhelming.

items.definitionEn: an activity you do regularly for pleasure rather than work
items.example: Gardening is her favourite pastime in spring.

items.definitionEn: to relax after stress or effort
items.example: A hot bath helps me unwind after a noisy household evening.

items.definitionEn: a person who spends too much time sitting and watching screens
items.example: A couch potato rarely joins the Sunday walk.

items.definitionEn: to start a hobby or activity
items.example: She wants to take up pottery this autumn.

items.definitionEn: very interested in or enthusiastic about something
items.example: He is keen on board games more than football.

items.definitionEn: very enthusiastic; doing something as often as possible
items.example: She is an avid reader of family sagas.

items.definitionEn: a regular job done to keep a home running
items.example: Taking out the rubbish is his household chore this month.

items.definitionEn: time when you are not working or busy and can rest
items.example: Even busy parents need downtime without a to-do list.

items.definitionEn: to rest so that you feel energetic again
items.example: A quiet weekend in the countryside helps her recharge.

items.definitionEn: to watch many episodes of a series one after another
items.example: We binge-watch old sitcoms when the weather is dreadful.

items.definitionEn: to do small, pleasant jobs at home in a relaxed way
items.example: On Sunday mornings I potter about in the kitchen.

items.definitionEn: to spend time in a pleasant, unhurried way
items.example: They while away winter evenings with cards and tea.

items.definitionEn: repairing or decorating your home yourself instead of paying a professional
items.example: He spends rainy Sundays on DIY in the spare room.

items.definitionEn: a feeling that your life or hobbies are meaningful and satisfying
items.example: Creative hobbies can bring more fulfilment than shopping.

items.definitionEn: a person who prefers staying at home to going out
items.example: A homebody may still enjoy guests, just not noisy clubs.

items.definitionEn: a person who loves going to parties and staying out late
items.example: A party animal in the family can exhaust quieter relatives.

items.term: life and soul of the party
items.definitionEn: the person who makes a social event lively and fun
items.example: Uncle Tom is the life and soul of the party at every wedding.

items.definitionEn: someone who stays at the edge of a party and does not join in
items.example: A wallflower still deserves to be invited and spoken to.

items.definitionEn: a person who moves easily from group to group and loves socialising
items.example: A social butterfly fills the calendar with birthdays and coffees.

items.definitionEn: a person who lives a very private life and avoids other people
items.example: After the divorce he lived almost like a recluse for a year.

items.definitionEn: to be accepted because you seem similar to the others
items.example: Teenagers may change their clothes just to fit in.

items.definitionEn: not included in a group or activity
items.example: She felt left out when the group chat went silent.

items.definitionEn: polite, light conversation about unimportant topics
items.example: Some guests hate small talk and prefer a real discussion.

items.definitionEn: an informal meeting of friends or relatives
items.example: We have a family get-together on the first Sunday of the month.

items.definitionEn: to stop thinking about work or worries; to turn a device off
items.example: I switch off my phone after nine so the evening stays calm.

items.definitionEn: the amount of time spent looking at phones, tablets or televisions
items.example: Parents argue about screen time more than about pocket money.

items.definitionEn: a period when you avoid phones and other devices on purpose
items.example: A weekend digital detox made the walk feel longer and better.

items.definitionEn: to refuse to accept unfair treatment or pressure
items.example: You should stand up to friends who mock your hobbies.

items.definitionEn: to relax once the working day is over
items.example: He likes to unwind after work with a long walk.

items.definitionEn: the time when a young person is legally or socially recognised as an adult
items.example: A coming of age party marked her eighteenth birthday.

items.definitionEn: formal expressions of sympathy after someone has died
items.example: Please accept my condolences on the loss of your grandfather.

items.definitionEn: a party to celebrate moving into a new home
items.example: Bring a plant to the housewarming rather than more crockery.

items.definitionEn: a party for a man before he gets married, usually with male friends
items.example: The stag do was a walking weekend, not a nightclub crawl.

items.definitionEn: a party for a woman before she gets married, usually with female friends
items.example: The hen do stayed in a cottage by the sea.

items.definitionEn: the meal and party after a marriage ceremony
items.example: Speeches at the wedding reception made several guests cry.

items.definitionEn: to invite guests to raise their glasses and wish someone well
items.example: The father will propose a toast after the first course.

items.definitionEn: the state of having lost a close person through death
items.example: Colleagues gave her time off for bereavement.

items.definitionEn: the period and customs of showing sadness after a death
items.example: Black clothes are still a sign of mourning at many funerals.

items.definitionEn: an important event that marks progress in a life
items.example: Graduation felt like a milestone for the whole household.

items.definitionEn: a ceremony or experience that marks a new stage of life
items.example: Passing the driving test is a modern rite of passage.

items.definitionEn: a Christian ceremony in which a baby is named and welcomed
items.example: The whole family travelled for the christening.

items.definitionEn: to celebrate or remember a date each year
items.example: They mark an anniversary of their first meeting with a picnic.

items.definitionEn: the promises a couple make to each other during the ceremony
items.example: They wrote their own wedding vows instead of using the traditional ones.

items.definitionEn: a government office where civil marriages and births are recorded
items.example: They booked the registry office for a Friday afternoon.

items.definitionEn: a legal wedding without a religious service
items.example: A civil ceremony can still feel personal and serious.

items.definitionEn: a date you remember each year because something important happened then
items.example: Their tenth anniversary will be spent in the same seaside town.

items.definitionEn: an occasion when relatives meet together
items.example: A family gathering at Easter includes aunts from both sides.

items.definitionEn: the group of people you spend time with socially
items.example: A supportive circle of friends makes the exam year easier.

items.definitionEn: time spent doing something for your own rest or hobby
items.example: She blocks an hour of me time every Saturday morning.
